# The timeline draws its body gridlines off its header ticks

## Context

Three seats hit this between 2026-11-20 and 11-21 while building the Engine 14 timeline examples: defect-notes from Ada (`gantt/taskColumns` draft) and Vega (`scheduler/eventEditor`, #21615), and #21694 (`scheduler/liveUpdates`) works around it. Measured headless at `208e95abd4` (the `dev` engine), `neo-theme-neo-dark`, 1440 × 900: the step the track resolves against the spacing of the header's minor ticks.

| Example | Declares the step | Track resolves | Minor ticks |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scheduler/nonWorkingTime` | 68 px on `.site-viewport` | 120 px | 68 px |
| `gantt/workingTime` | 53 px on `.kitchen-viewport` | 120 px | 53 px |
| `gantt/basic` | nothing | 120 px | 172.8 px |
| `scheduler/basic` | nothing | 120 px | 60 px |
| `scheduler/barRenderer` | 120 px | 120 px | 120 px |
| `scheduler/liveUpdates` (#21694) | 270 px on `.neo-timeline-track` | 270 px | 270 px |

## The Problem

In four of the six examples the body's gridlines fall between the header's ticks, so the chart reads as misdrawn. An example that wants aligned lines must compute `pxPerMinute × tick minutes` by hand for every breakpoint, and a value set on its viewport never reaches the track.

## The Architectural Reality

- `resources/css/src/timeline/Column.css` draws the lines as a repeating gradient keyed on `var(--neo-timeline-gridline-step, 120px)`.
- Every theme declares `--neo-timeline-gridline-step: 120px` in `:where(.neo-theme-<name>)` (`resources/css/theme-neo-dark/timeline/Column.css`), and `.neo-grid-view` carries the theme class, so the grid view re-declares 120 px between the example's viewport and the track.
- Nothing derives the step. `Neo.timeline.TimeAxis` owns `pxPerMinute`, `tickUnit` and `tickStep`, and `Neo.timeline.Column` already writes inline custom properties on its track (`--neo-timeline-track-x`).
- Four examples set the variable by hand, with values per media query: `scheduler/nonWorkingTime`, `scheduler/barRenderer`, `scheduler/meridian` (`calc(100% / 7)`) and `gantt/workingTime`.
- Design authority: n/a — gridlines off their ticks are no behaviour anyone intends; the variable names the tick step.

## The Fix

- `Neo.timeline.Column` writes `--neo-timeline-gridline-step` inline on its track from its axis: the minor tick's width in px when the tick unit has a fixed length (minute, hour, day, week), recomputed when the axis' `pxPerMinute`, `tickUnit` or `tickStep` changes (zoom included). For `month` it writes nothing, and the theme default applies.
- The four examples (and #21694's, if it merges first) drop their hand-set values.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] In `scheduler/basic`, `scheduler/nonWorkingTime`, `gantt/basic` and `gantt/workingTime`, the track's resolved step equals the header's minor-tick spacing at 1440 × 900, at 390 × 844 and after a zoom (e2e, red on `dev`).
- [ ] No example sets `--neo-timeline-gridline-step`.
- [ ] Frames of `gantt/basic` and `scheduler/nonWorkingTime`, before and after, in a dark and a light theme.

## Out of Scope

- Month ticks, whose widths differ: they keep the theme default.
- The calendar's own time scale.

## Avoided Traps

- Moving the theme default to the document root only: an example's value would then reach the track, but every example would still compute the step by hand.
